subject: MAP contingency trigger — procurement unblock required to avoid close slip
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@everhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP contingency trigger — procurement unblock required to avoid close slip

Samantha — following our call earlier, flagging a hard blocker in your procurement review that will push out the go-live if not resolved by June 17.

Quick summary:
- Procurement requires a revised SOW with the data retention term clarified (EverHealth asked for 12 months; standard is 30 days).
- Legal sign-off gating is on the SOW version change; procurement is not routing without procurement@everhealth confirmation.

From our side I propose two parallel actions:
1) We prepare a redline SOW that uses a contractual compromise (30 day default + carve for PHI logs retained 12 months on encrypted store).
2) If procurement can issue a conditional PO or written go-ahead to allow our onboarding to proceed while legal finishes the final SOW, we can keep the June 30 close.

I attached an updated MAP worksheet (EverHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx) with contingencies and an adjusted timeline. Please confirm the procurement point of contact and whether a conditional PO is feasible.

Thanks,
Jonas
---
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@everhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam Park <liam.park@everhealth.com>, EverHealth Procurement <procurement@everhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP contingency trigger — procurement unblock required to avoid close slip

Jonas — thanks for the note and the MAP. I escalated to procurement and legal. Two quick updates:
- Procurement confirms they need the SOW finalized to issue a PO; they cannot issue a conditional PO per policy. (Sorry — that’s on us.)
- Legal is open to a 12-month retention carve for PHI logs, but we need a short justification memo from your side describing how those logs are protected and access controls.

I can get legal to review a one-page tech note if you send it today; procurement will then prioritize the PO.

Samantha
Samantha Cho
Director of Partnerships | EverHealth
samantha.cho@everhealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: EverHealth Procurement <procurement@everhealth.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@everhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP contingency trigger — procurement unblock required to avoid close slip

Thanks Samantha — understood on the procurement policy. Marissa and Camila: can we get the one-page technical memo drafted today outlining encryption at rest, key management, role-based access, and audit logging? I think that addresses legal’s ask and keeps us on the June 30 target if legal signs off fast.

Camila — I'll need a prioritized checklist for onboarding tasks we can begin before the PO arrives (sandbox access, model deployment prep, pre-provisioning of tokenized test datasets). Can you add estimated lead times to each item in the MAP?

Ben — heads up: if legal delays beyond Wed (June 11), I will recommend we escalate to procurement leadership for an exception request.

Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP contingency trigger — procurement unblock required to avoid close slip

On it. Drafted the tech memo and attached a PDF (Procurement_SOW_comments.pdf) with the SOW redline and a short security summary.

Key bullets in the memo:
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, customer-specific KMS integration (customer-managed keys supported).
- Access: strict RBAC, time-limited admin tokens for onboarding, SOC2 controls referenced.
- Audit: immutable audit trail for data access, logs retained 12 months for PHI-only fields; metadata logs default 30 days.

Camila — I've also updated the MAP with a two-track onboarding plan:
A) Pre-PO sandbox tasks (can start immediately, low-risk): sandbox provisioning, basic integration tests, review sessions.
B) Post-PO production tasks: final data syncs, production model deployment, SLA activation.

I added estimated lead times (sandbox: 3 business days; prod deploy: 8 business days after PO).

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: EverHealth Procurement <procurement@everhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Request for procurement prioritization — EVH-2025-087 (EverHealth)

Hi procurement team — Ben Carter from Redwood here. Appreciate the earlier notes. We submitted the redline SOW and a one-page technical memo (attached by Marissa). Given the mutual action plan and the commercial schedule we discussed, could you advise the minimum gating approvals required to release a PO or an approval memo so onboarding can commence?

Ask:
- If a conditional PO is prohibited, would a procurement-signed approval memo (email accepted) reserving funds and confirming intent suffice to let us begin sandbox provisioning?
- If not, can you provide the exact steps and expected turnaround so we can re-baseline the MAP and communicate a revised close date to stakeholders?

We want to avoid a slip to July. Please route to your procurement lead — copying Jonas and Marissa for context.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Liam Park <liam.park@everhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@everhealth.com>, EverHealth Procurement <procurement@everhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for procurement prioritization — EVH-2025-087 (EverHealth)

Ben/Jonas — quick update from procurement lead (on behalf of procurement):
- We cannot issue a PO without the fully-executed SOW. We can, however, provide a written procurement intent email that confirms budget and prioritization; that should allow limited sandbox provisioning per our internal rules.
- Legal wants the tech memo and the SOW redline; once legal signs (target Wed EOD) procurement will issue the PO the following day.

Next steps agreed:
1) Redwood provides the tech memo + final SOW redline (done).
2) EverHealth legal to sign by Wed EOD (internal).
3) Procurement to send procurement intent email to Jonas by Thu morning; PO to follow on Thu evening.

If timeline holds we can keep the June 30 close; if legal slips we will need to re-baseline and schedule a short exec sync. Will notify both teams by Thu noon if anything changes.

Liam Park
Procurement Program Manager | EverHealth
liam.park@everhealth.com
End of thread: internal follow-ups tracked in MAP; attachments: EverHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx, Procurement_SOW_comments.pdf
